test_title: SSC CGL 2024 Tier-II Official Paper-I (Held On: 20 Jan, 2025)
subject: general
question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.

Kanhaiya said to me, “Do you want to sing?”

options.text: Kanhaiya said that I would sing or not
Kanhaiya said that whether I would sing
Kanhaiya asked me if I wanted to sing.
Kanhaiya enquires if I want to sing.

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indirect Speech:** Kanhaiya asked me if I wanted to sing.
 
• **Direct to Indirect Speech:** 
 
 
• **Reporting Verb Change:** 
 
 
• 'said to' is changed to 'asked' to indicate a question.
 
 
 
• **Pronoun Change:** 
 
 
• "you" is changed to "I" to match the perspective of the person being addressed.
 
 
 
• **Tense Change:** 
 
 
• "want" is changed to "wanted" to reflect the past tense in reported speech.
 
 
 
• **Question Word Change:** 
 
 
• "Do" is omitted and replaced by "if" to form an indirect question.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Punctuation and Format:**
 
 
• No quotation marks are used in indirect speech.
 
• The reporting clause "Kanhaiya asked me if..." starts the sentence.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Kanhaiya asked me if I wanted to sing."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "Kanhaiya said that I would sing or not"

 
 
• Does not properly convert the question into reported speech.
 
• The phrase "would sing or not" is not correctly framed and doesn't make sense in the context.
 
 
 
• **Option 2:** "Kanhaiya said that whether I would sing"
 
 
• Incorrectly frames the indirect speech by using "said that whether" instead of "asked if."
 
• The sentence structure is incomplete and does not convey the original intent properly.
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** "Kanhaiya enquires if I want to sing."
 
 
• Uses "enquires" instead of "asked," which is less common in everyday usage, especially in past tense reporting.
 
• Fails to change "want" to "wanted" to reflect the past tense in reported speech.
